accuracy.evidence: Matched to NC Y1 number and place value (count in multiples of 2, 5 and 10; given a number, identify one more) and the EYFS ELG on counting patterns; the topic's own evidence lists (2s odd/even, +1 next number, +10 moves down a row on a hundred chart) are each a lab step. Checked by hand: 5 pairs = 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 = 10 in 1s; 5+1, 12+1, 19+1 = 6, 13, 20; 23, 33, 43 sit in one column of a 10-wide square; hops of 2 from 1 give 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 (never 10); 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 end 5, 0, 5, 0; towers 2, 4, 6, 8, 10; challenge answers 10, 33, 20, 9, 17, 8, 50.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early counting slips: believing a different counting method changes the total (conservation, step 1 prediction), counting groups not items (4 pairs said as 4, tag pairs), adding 1 instead of the step when continuing a skip count (16 after 15, tag one), moving across instead of down on a hundred square (24 for 23 + 10, tag side), jumping too far (tag skip) and breaking the odd pattern when counting in 2s from 1 (tag odd).

lab_distinct.evidence: flageffic is about using a repeat to save work: tap-to-count pairs with the 1s total confirmed, a +1 number track over three rounds, a 1–50 hundred square where only the square straight below counts, a frog that can only reach odd landings, hands counted in 5s with a next-number pick, and towers predicted before they are built. flagpat and flagabab are shape repeat patterns, flagfours is 4s, 8s, 50s and 100s; the shingle gate is under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner does the counting and the result appears on the canvas before any rule is stated: the 2s total sits beside the 1s count, the hundred square lights the column 23, 33, 43, the frog's landings show only odd numbers, the hand totals expose the 5, 0 endings, and tower 5 is built only after the learner predicts it. Step text then confirms the shortcut.

predictions.evidence: Six predictions with a tempting wrong option each: 'No, you get more' (counting in 2s seems to give a different total), 18 for 19 + 1, 'Next to 23' for 23 + 10, 'Yes, soon' for landing on 10, 21 after 20 in the 5s count, and 8 for tower 5 (the next tower, not the fifth).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge items, each with two tagged wrong answers (one, skip, side, back, odd, pairs); every message names the slip, e.g. 'That is 1 more. 10 more is one row down: the tens go up, the ones stay the same.' and 'You counted the pairs. Each pair is 2 socks: 2, 4, 6, 8.'

readability.evidence: Kid text uses very short sentences and words a 5-year-old hears in class (pairs, count in 2s, 1 more, next, pattern, hundred square). The adult text was rewritten into shorter sentences after the first validate run reported FK 14.2, and now passes the family limits.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate clean. Each kid paragraph carries one idea (groups let you skip count, the total stays the same, +1 and +10 patterns, patterns predict), and each lab step practises one idea from the topic's evidence list.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 dark and 360 px Android light screenshots after Show me on every step. Young mode gives 56 px DOM buttons for every answer; the hundred-square cells are small (about 30 px) so each round also offers three big answer buttons; the tower layout was moved up after the first shot showed the message overlapping the tower labels, and the long +1 heading was shortened.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas tap has a button twin (Count a pair, three answer buttons for +1 and +10, Hop to n, Count a hand, 21/25/30, 8/10/12); the canvas aria-label is updated with every spoken result, including challenge feedback; walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone.
